commit_message:
[Merged] [sfnt] `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` can now also load a font's table directory.

Closes issue #1263.

* src/sfnt/ttload.c (tt_face_load_any): Implement it.

intro_commit_message:
[sfnt] `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` can now also load a font's table directory.

Closes issue #1263.

* src/sfnt/ttload.c (tt_face_load_any): Implement it.
fix_commit_message:
src/sfnt/ttload.c (tt_face_load_any): Correctly handle font containers.

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/424613326
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d3668e00da73 on top of intro 5a07f41d0edd via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): An out-of-bounds read vulnerability exists in the `tt_face_load_any` function in `src/sfnt/ttload.c`. When `FT_Load_Sfnt_Table` is called with `tag == 1` (requesting the font's table directory), the code indexes into `face->ttc_header.offsets[]` using `face->root.face_index & 0xFFFF` without checking whether the index is within the bounds of the `offsets` array (i.e., less than `face->ttc_header.count`). Because `face_index` is also used to enumerate elements of font containers such as Mac Resource files that are not TTC collections, the index can exceed the number of valid entries, leading to an out-of-bounds memory read. Root cause: The code introduced to implement table-directory access (tag == 1) assumed the face is always part of a TTC and that `face_index` is always a valid index into `ttc_header.offsets`. However, `face_index` is also used for non-TTC container formats (e.g., Mac Resource), and no bounds check was added before dereferencing the `offsets` array. The same oversight exists in `sfobjs.c` where a similar condition (`face_index >= face->ttc_header.count`) needed a comment clarifying the context.
